system.summary: Confederate Vigenere on the tabula recta with the key COMERETRIBUTION, enciphering only chosen words of otherwise clear telegrams; the key runs over the cipher letters only and restarts at offset 0 with each telegram.
system.sibling_key: COMERETRIBUTION, one of the three known Confederate keys; COMPLETEVICTORY and MANCHESTERBLUFF tested as controls. The catalogue's OCR triage suggests COMPLETE VICTORY in vol. 10 (not checked here).
system.notes: Distinct symbols: the 26-letter alphabet of the tabula recta. The clerks' capitals mislead in a few recurring ways (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, a U-like glyph for IC); every correction is a single glyph and is listed in alignment.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Two of the four telegrams (6 and 8 April 1865) are printed in clear in War of the Rebellion: Official Records, Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 (1897), pp. 1209 and 1216. The 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in OR I/49 pts. 1-2.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue item; transcription, decryption, controls and the prior-art search were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the NARA catalogue records of vols. 196, 11 and 10 and the full-resolution frames listed in the catalogue's OCR run lists; screened them on montages. Vol. 196 frame 0027 has no cipher words (an OCR false hit).
Read the cipher words of vol. 196 fr. 0061 (180 letters) and vol. 11 frs. 0022, 0036 and 0039 (52, 56 and 61 letters) and the clear text around them from the images.

Applied the known Confederate key COMERETRIBUTION, over the cipher letters only, offset 0 at each telegram: English from the first letter in all four telegrams (171/180, 50/52, 46/57, 59/61 letters right as read).

Explained the remaining letters as single misleading glyphs of the clerks' capitals (barred E for F, T for F, R for J, N for G, Y for V, X for W, Z for E, U for M, C for B, U-like glyph for IC); no correction needs more than one glyph.

Controls on the letters as read (decrypt.py --controls): COMERETRIBUTION offset 0 chi2 19-37; best other offset 92-676; COMPLETEVICTORY 132-381; MANCHESTERBLUFF 133-1072; 200 random keys minimum 75-402; shuffled cipher words with the right key 3-10 letters agreeing on average.

OCR full text of OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 searched for each plaintext phrase: the 6 April telegram to Levy is printed in clear on p. 1209. The 12 and 30 March and 8 April telegrams not found in this first search.

Second, independent agent: re-read all four telegrams on its own crops, decrypted them with its own code (same plaintext, 171/180, 50/52, 59/61 letters right as read), corrected the 12 March letter count to 180, read the 8 April date line, and found that the 8 April telegram is printed in clear in OR I/49/2 p. 1216 (the first search missed it because of double spaces in the OCR text). Searched OR I/49 pt. 1 for the 12 March telegram: not found.
The four telegrams written as sentences (<doc>_reading.md). One hole: [?west] in the 12 March telegram, where the cipher gives WEST and the sense wants 'what'.

outcome.method_basis: The key COMERETRIBUTION was already identified for this correspondence: catalogue entry 681 had read frame 0061 and the vol. 11 OCR runs with it, and it is the known key of Confederate telegraph traffic in 1864-65. It was applied to each telegram from its first cipher letter, word by word; two of the four telegrams are printed in clear in OR I/49/2.
outcome.notes: Four telegrams read (350 cipher letters); the 6 April telegram needed 11 of its 57 letters corrected and is settled only with the clear text printed in OR I/49/2 p. 1209; the other cipher passages of vols. 10, 11 and 196 are not read. Two of the four are earlier solutions (OR I/49/2 pp. 1209, 1216); the 12 and 30 March telegrams were not found in print. fraction_read is unknown because the unread passages have not been transcribed or counted.

texts.label: Taylor (W. F. Bullock Jr.) to Maury, Meridian, 12 Mar 1865, vol. 196 fr. 0061
texts.summary: At the start of Canby's campaign against Mobile, Taylor asks Maury to report in cipher the cavalry on each side of Mobile Bay, its strength and commander, to keep the cavalry close to the enemy and in telegraphic touch with D. W. Adams and headquarters, and to name a point outside the city for a courier line.
texts.note: read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: 1 hole in 89 words.

texts.label: Surget to Taylor, Meridian, 30 Mar 1865, vol. 11 fr. 0022
texts.summary: Surget reports to Taylor the forwarding of Lee's and Pillow's despatches, a (false) report that Sherman had been wounded, and the permission for Federal ambulances between Big Black and Jackson; in cipher he asks that the War Department again be urged to relieve Col. Watts (probably N. G. Watts, the agent of exchange), whose habits unfit him for the position.
texts.note: read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: no holes in 102 words.

texts.label: Surget to Levy, Meridian, 6 Apr 1865, vol. 11 fr. 0036
texts.summary: Surget tells Levy at Mobile, in cipher, to see that Sam Duncan returns promptly, which is to his advantage, and adds in clear that the enemy (Wilson's raid) seem to have crossed the river at Selma going east.
texts.note: Earlier solution: OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 p. 1209. read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: no holes in 47 words.

texts.label: Surget to Taylor, Meridian, 8 Apr 1865, vol. 11 fr. 0039
texts.summary: Surget passes on to Taylor at Demopolis the news, from Northern papers received by General Hodge, that Richmond fell by assault on 3 April 1865.
texts.note: Earlier solution: OR Ser. I vol. 49 pt. 2 p. 1216. read_share from research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: no holes in 31 words.
